label: unseen leg landed; rest running
result: On the unseen exam it solved 186 of 200 -- a new program best (pure-subgoal planners: 175-177) -- and narrowed the move-count gap to the move-by-move (forward) planner from 2.2 extra moves to 1.2 on puzzles both solve (loss ratio improved from 3/43 to 5/31). 36 of 200 puzzles were won by a 'slide one robot first, then plan' solution. Every composed solution replay-validated.
conclusion: The most promising result of the program so far -- the first crack in the subgoal language ceiling. Standard-search control and standard-exam legs still running; final verdict pending those. Caveat: the forward baseline here is the original network; a carefully re-tuned forward planner would likely solve a few more puzzles and could narrow this gap measurement slightly -- at the size where re-tuning was tried (smaller boards, 8 robots), it gained 8 hard puzzles out of 184 (main FINDINGS 24).
